title: Write in Spoken Language
summary: Argues that writing should match spoken language patterns rather than formal written conventions; recommends reading drafts aloud and asking whether each sentence would be spoken to a friend to improve clarity and reader engagement.
when-to-read: Read this when you're writing documentation, guides, or explanations and want to make your content more accessible and engaging to readers. If you're looking for guidance on structuring longer documents or organizing complex information architecturally, consult documentation or technical-writing resources instead.
